recommendation: MONTHLY tenor: manage with the delta-band roll (|delta|>=0.30, max 3 rolls), NOT stop-2x. Stop-2x registered-MISSed both edges of its bar (F16: worst-month cut 46.0% vs bar >=50%, mean cost 32.2% vs bar <=30%) and is not promotable; the roll delivers a 35.5% worst-month cut at 9.6% mean cost -- 0.27 cost-per-pp-of-cut vs the stop's 0.70 (2.6x more efficient, c03.py) -- and the best p5 left tail of the three variants (-1.044 %S vs hold -2.528). Caveat: the roll is an UNBARRED descriptive cell; before any promotion it needs its own pre-registered bar in a new trial (H60-VRP design brief). WEEKLY tenor: NO daily-close management rule is adequate -- the F17 close-stop buys only a 7% worst-week improvement (-100% -> -93.3%) at 11% mean cost (cost-per-pp 1.57, ~6x worse than the monthly roll) and its stopped arm still compounds to -28.96%/yr; F15 shows why structurally: at 7d the stop-2x gap-through threshold is only 2.0-5.2% (vs 3.9-10.2% at 30d), measured P(gap-through) is 0.55-2.01%/day (vs 0.00-0.25% at 30d), and a gapped exit averages 2.9x credit (max ~8.6-9.0x) against the intended 2x. Weekly risk is gamma/gap risk (2.1x gamma at 0.48x vega of 30d) that no close-based stop can see; if weekly is traded at all, the binding control is SIZING (F17: the compounding RUIN is sizing-dependent, not frequency-dependent; F18's DD-constrained f=0.035/wk), plus the 2.5-sigma wings themselves. Net adjudication for the H60-VRP brief: monthly + delta-band roll as the management default to be bar-registered; weekly only as a sized, wing-defined structure with no stop credited for tail protection.
